Currency: EUR excl. VAT (the site adds 20% VAT for the viewer region shown); converted at 1.17 USD/EUR.
Traffic: 10 TB/month per Mac included (1 Gbit/s); M2 Pro plans 30 TB (10 Gbit/s). Overage EUR 5/TB excl. VAT; email at 80%; speed limit possible on request instead.

fleet.verification: Payment card; automated anti-fraud checks may request extra verification. Provider says such checks usually take minutes, not a quota-increase SLA.
fleet.notes: Dedicated Mac hosting; every SKU out of stock 2026-09-29. Servers cannot be created via API ('The automated creation of servers is currently not supported'; API is beta: list servers, power, firewall). ToS 3.11 allows unpublished per-account limits on servers/traffic; ToS 2.5 automated ID verification if fraud risk. Bulk orders via contact.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Do you offer backups? Since our Macs are dedicated devices, our customers are responsible for their own backups.
snapshot_auto.note: Dedicated bare-metal Mac mini, always on; no pause/sleep/checkpoint concept. Only DIY Time Machine to the network-storage add-on.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Since our Macs are dedicated devices, our customers are responsible for their own backups. We do however offer affordable network storage with Time Machine support, allowing you to set up automated Time Machine backups.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/image endpoints in the Customer API (only servers, power actions, firewalls); no snapshot feature in panel docs. Time Machine backups (scheduled, file-level, DIY) mentioned only.

harness_api.quote: OakHost offers an API to access and manipulate your resources, such as server information, firewall and more. [...] The automated creation of servers is currently not supported.
harness_api.note: OpenAPI spec has only GET /servers, /servers/{id}, firewall CRUD/assign, and /servers/{id}/action (reboot/power/force_off/force_reboot/shutdown). 'OakHost Agent' is an optional monitoring/power daemon, not an AI agent.

egress_allowlist.quote: Outbound Rules define traffic that is initiated from your server. [...] By default, all traffic will be blocked, except for the defined rules. That means that an empty ruleset on an active firewall denys all incoming and outgoing connections.
egress_allowlist.note: External hardware firewall (Customer Panel or API), outbound rules by IPv4/IPv6 address/CIDR/range + ports + tcp/udp/icmp. Default ruleset allows all outbound; editable to default-deny. Firewall is optional (no assigned firewall = all traffic passes). Changes take up to 30 s; stateful.

egress_http_rules.note: Firewall rule schema has only type (inbound/outbound), position, ipv4_addresses, ipv6_addresses, ports, protocol (tcp/udp/icmp), comment. L3/L4 only, no HTTP-level rules.

ingress_rules.quote: Inbound Rules define any traffic that comes from the internet to your server. For example, connecting to the Screen Sharing or SSH service on your server from your local PC falls into this category.
ingress_rules.note: Inbound rules by source IP/CIDR/range, ports, protocol; default firewall template allows only SSH and Screen Sharing inbound. Static public IPv4. No preview URLs / HTTPS proxy.

guest_firewall.note: Dedicated physical Mac mini with full admin/root and Recovery Mode access (SIP can be disabled); macOS includes pf (pfctl) and the application firewall. Firewall docs themselves suggest 'Consider deploying a software firewall' when no external firewall is assigned. Not nftables/iptables (macOS).

secret_proxy.quote: OakHost offers an API to access and manipulate your resources, such as server information, firewall and more.
secret_proxy.note: No credential-injection/HTTP-proxy product exists anywhere in the docs or API surface (which covers only servers, power actions, and firewall rules); this is a plain dedicated-hardware host where any secrets live on the machine itself, not a false-by-definition absence but confirmed by the exhaustive, small API surface.

volume_attach.quote: Network Storage can be ordered as an add-on for server subscriptions and comes in various different storage tiers. It can be accessed via the SMB protocol
volume_attach.note: SMB network share (not block volume), reachable only from OakHost internal network; each product has own username/password; pitched for Time Machine backups. Pricing not captured here.

volume_shared.quote: If you have multiple servers at OakHost, all servers can access the network storage, to enable easy file sharing between devices.
volume_shared.note: Read-write SMB share mountable concurrently by several of the customer's Macs.

isolation.note: Whole dedicated physical Mac mini per customer (root/admin, no hypervisor layer between customer and hardware).

image_oci.quote: Dedicated Mac mini hosting on macOS Tahoe in Germany, ready to go within minutes - with full access through your browser.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - a dedicated bare-metal Mac ships with a stock macOS install; there is no OCI/Docker image boot mechanism anywhere in the docs or Customer API.

docker_inside.quote: Jenkins needs to be installed using Homebrew, a package manager for macOS. The installation is quite straight-forward
docker_inside.note: derived: customer has full root/admin on real Apple hardware and can install anything via Homebrew (as shown in the Jenkins tutorial), including Docker Desktop for Mac, exactly as on any owned Mac. Not a provider-managed feature, just consequence of full root access.

anti_bot.quote: Dedicated Mac mini hosting on macOS Tahoe in Germany, ready to go within minutes - with full access through your browser.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - this is dedicated Mac hardware hosting (CI/dev/build machines), not a browser/scraping automation product; no stealth/fingerprinting feature exists.

captcha_solving.quote: Dedicated Mac mini hosting on macOS Tahoe in Germany, ready to go within minutes - with full access through your browser.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - dedicated Mac hardware host, not a browser-automation/agent product; no CAPTCHA feature anywhere in docs.

egress_ip_type.quote: All of our devices have pre-allocated public-facing IP addresses. One IPv4 address per device, as well as a /64 IPv6 address space. These IPs are publicly accessible, but can easily be firewalled for added security. The country associated with the IPs is Germany.
egress_ip_type.note: Fixed, dedicated public IPv4 (and IPv6 /64) per physical Mac in an OakHost German datacenter; matches static_egress_ip: true already recorded on the card.

live_resize.note: CPU/RAM are fixed to the physical Mac mini model/configuration ordered (M1/M2/M4 variants with fixed core counts and soldered RAM); changing size means ordering a different physical device, not resizing a running machine.

own_agent_api.quote: OakHost offers an API to access and manipulate your resources, such as server information, firewall and more. [...] The automated creation of servers is currently not supported.
own_agent_api.note: Customer API only exposes server listing, firewall CRUD, and power actions (reboot/shutdown/force-off); no browser/computer-use/research agent product or API exists.

mcp_server.quote: For a complete list of endpoints, please refer to the Swagger documentation.
mcp_server.note: No MCP server mentioned in docs, GitHub, or the Customer API reference; only a REST/Swagger API for firewall and power management.

lang_python.quote: Jenkins needs to be installed using Homebrew, a package manager for macOS.
lang_python.note: Ships as a stock macOS install; Python is not preinstalled/managed by OakHost out of the box - customers install their own toolchain via Homebrew, as shown in the tutorials.

lang_node.quote: Jenkins needs to be installed using Homebrew, a package manager for macOS.
lang_node.note: Ships as a stock macOS install; Node.js is not preinstalled/managed by OakHost out of the box - customers install their own toolchain via Homebrew, as shown in the tutorials.

soc2.quote: Our data centers are located in Nuremberg and Bamberg in Germany, fully DIN ISO/IEC 27001 certified and powered by 100% green energy.
soc2.note: Only ISO/IEC 27001 certification is claimed for the datacenters; no SOC 2 attestation is mentioned anywhere on the site, docs, or ToS.

hipaa.quote: Dedicated Mac mini hosting on macOS Tahoe in Germany, ready to go within minutes - with full access through your browser.
hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - a small EU dedicated-Mac hosting company with no HIPAA/BAA mention anywhere in docs, ToS, or marketing.

sso.note: Customer Panel login is standard account-based (email/password); no SAML/OIDC SSO offering mentioned anywhere in docs or account/user-management pages.

max_session_h.quote: Dedicated Mac mini hosting in the cloud in just a few seconds.
max_session_h.note: Primary product (always-on-commit) is a dedicated physical Mac that stays on and reachable until the customer cancels the subscription (min 1-month term, auto-extends); no forced session/runtime limit. The separate one-off 7-day trial plan is capped at 168h but is not the modeled always-on product.

volumes.quote: Network Storage can be ordered as an add-on for server subscriptions and comes in various different storage tiers. It can be accessed via the SMB protocol ... If you have multiple servers at OakHost, all servers can access the network storage, to enable easy file sharing between devices.
volumes.note: Contradiction confirmed: OakHost sells an attachable, cross-server SMB 'Network Storage' add-on (volume_attach=true, volume_shared=true already in card), so volumes=false is wrong; correct value is true.

snapshot.quote: Do you offer backups? Since our Macs are dedicated devices, our customers are responsible for their own backups. We do however offer affordable network storage with Time Machine support, allowing you to set up automated Time Machine backups.
snapshot.note: No provider-side snapshot/image capability; only DIY Time Machine backups to the separate network-storage add-on, and the Customer API exposes no snapshot/image endpoints (only server list, power actions, firewall).

pause_resume.quote: OakHost offers an API to access and manipulate your resources, such as server information, firewall and more. [...] The automated creation of servers is currently not supported.
pause_resume.note: OakHost sells a whole dedicated always-on Mac mini (bare metal, billed monthly regardless of use); the only lifecycle actions exposed are power on/off/reboot, not a pause/resume that reduces billing. No pause/resume feature is documented anywhere.

fork.quote: The automated creation of servers is currently not supported.
fork.note: There is no clone/fork mechanism: the API can't even create servers automatically, let alone clone an existing machine's disk/state into a new one.

fork_running.quote: The automated creation of servers is currently not supported.
fork_running.note: No fork capability at all (see fork), so cloning a running machine without stopping it is not offered either.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: The automated creation of servers is currently not supported.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No snapshot or fork feature exists (see snapshot/fork), so memory-inclusive fork is also not offered.

computer_use.quote: OakHost offers an API to access and manipulate your resources, such as server information, firewall and more.
computer_use.note: Customer API only manages power state and firewall rules; there is no screenshot/click driving API. Desktop access is via standard macOS Screen Sharing (VNC/RDP-like), operated by the human user, not an automation API.

custom_image.quote: Bare Metal Mac mini Hosting All our tiers are backed by excellent support, world-class performance and genuine Apple-designed dedicated hardware.
custom_image.note: Servers are provisioned as physical Apple Mac minis running stock macOS; there is no documented mechanism to upload/boot a custom OS image (Apple's platform/SLA requires standard signed macOS), and the API only exposes existing server power/firewall actions, not imaging.

wake_on_request.quote: Since our Macs are dedicated devices, our customers are responsible for their own backups.
wake_on_request.note: Machines are dedicated always-on hardware billed monthly (requires_always_on); there is no sleep/idle-triggered-wake product, only manual power on/off via the API.

auto_stop_idle.quote: OakHost offers an API to access and manipulate your resources, such as server information, firewall and more.
auto_stop_idle.note: No idle-detection/auto-stop feature is documented; the dedicated-hardware billing model (monthly commitment, minimum 1-month term) is inherently always-on rather than usage/idle based.

inbound_https.quote: Inbound Rules define any traffic that comes from the internet to your server. For example, connecting to the Screen Sharing or SSH service on your server from your local PC falls into this category.
inbound_https.note: OakHost gives a raw static public IPv4 with an L3/L4 packet firewall (default template allows only SSH and Screen Sharing inbound); there is no managed HTTPS URL/proxy/ingress product -- customers would have to run and terminate their own TLS on the box.

agent_harnesses.quote: With our OakHost Agent, you can easily set up email alerts to get notified about performance issues or approaching disk limits, allowing you to catch potential issues... Announcing Advanced Mac Monitoring with OakHost Agent... This allows you to monitor CPU usage, memory consumption, and disk space directly.
agent_harnesses.note: The only thing called 'Agent' is an optional system-monitoring/alerting daemon; no coding agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) are preinstalled or offered as templates anywhere in the docs or product pages.

gpu.quote: Discover our macOS Cloud hosting plans. Experience fast performance, reliable uptime, and EU-based security for your Mac-powered business.
gpu.note: Product is dedicated Mac mini hosting (integrated Apple-Silicon GPU only, not sold/selectable as a discrete GPU tier); there is no GPU SKU or GPU-cloud offering -- outside what this product is.

windows.quote: Discover our macOS Cloud hosting plans. Experience fast performance, reliable uptime, and EU-based security for your Mac-powered business.
windows.note: OakHost exclusively hosts physical Apple Mac mini machines running macOS; Windows is not an offered OS -- outside what this product is.

self_host.quote: Bare Metal Mac mini Hosting All our tiers are backed by excellent support, world-class performance and genuine Apple-designed dedicated hardware.
self_host.note: OakHost is a hosting company that rents out its own physical Mac minis in its own EU datacenter; there is no software product you could self-host on your own infrastructure.

byoc.quote: Bare Metal Mac mini Hosting All our tiers are backed by excellent support, world-class performance and genuine Apple-designed dedicated hardware.
byoc.note: Machines are OakHost-owned dedicated hardware in OakHost's own EU facilities; it is not a managed service deployable into the customer's own cloud account.

open_source.quote: OakHost offers an API to access and manipulate your resources, such as server information, firewall and more.
open_source.note: OakHost is a proprietary commercial hosting business (ToS-governed subscription service); no OSI-licensed core product is published or referenced anywhere.

cpu_class.quote: Bare Metal Mac mini Hosting All our tiers are backed by excellent support, world-class performance and genuine Apple-designed dedicated hardware.
cpu_class.note: Each subscription (both the always-on-commit monthly plans and the one-off 'Try macOS for a week' trial) provisions a whole dedicated physical Mac mini per customer, with no hypervisor and no other tenant sharing that machine's cores; the entire chip's CPU cores are physically dedicated to the single lessee for the lease period, matching the card's isolation: 'bare-metal'.

usage_api.quote: OakHost offers an API to access and manipulate your resources, such as server information, firewall and more. The automated creation of servers is currently not supported.
usage_api.note: granularity: none; cost: no; OpenAPI specification lists only GET /servers, GET /servers/{id}, and firewall CRUD operations; no usage, billing, or cost endpoints exist. Usage is only available via the web-based customer panel or invoices.
